extracted.intended_audience: public company management, CFOs, corporate accounting and SEC filing preparers, auditors, and securities counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) required by Regulation S‑K, Item 303, including what trends, liquidity, critical accounting estimates, market risks, and climate-related matters to disclose and how to present them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise disclosure objective for MD&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise disclosure objective for MD&A as required by the SEC final rule updating Item 303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule codified a disclosure objective so registrants should focus MD&A on the objective of helping investors understand the registrant’s financial condition, results of operations, and material trends and uncertainties. Use the objective to shape which items are material and relevant to operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of known trends or uncertainties materially affecting revenues or income
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose “any known trends or uncertainties that have had or that are reasonably likely to have a material favorable or unfavorable impact on net sales or revenues or income from continuing operations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early‑warning disclosures should tell investors (1) when charges may be incurred (e.g., contingencies, restructurings, impairments), (2) when revenue growth or margins may be unsustainable, or (3) when debt covenant compliance may be at risk. See Item 303(b)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of known events reasonably likely to change cost‑to‑revenue relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any known events that are “reasonably likely to cause a material change in the relationship between costs and revenues (such as known or reasonably likely future increases in costs . . . ).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe events that could materially change cost/revenue relationships, quantify impacts where practicable, and explain management actions and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain reasons for significant period‑to‑period changes (quantitative and qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the reasons for significant changes in revenues, expenses, cash flows and financial position — not merely reciting amounts on the face of the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When more than one factor contributes to a change, quantify the impact of each component to enable investors to discern relative contributions (refer to SEC Release No. 33‑8350 and 33‑10890 and Item 303(b)(2)(iii)). Use both quantitative and qualitative explanations and, where meaningful, segment‑level analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify component drivers when multiple factors affect a change
rubrics_metrics.description: When a change is attributed to more than one factor (e.g., “primarily” one factor, “partially offset” by another), registrants should quantify each material component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of disclosure to demonstrate how each component will be quantified in future filings. Use tables or breakout disclosure when helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present changes in tabular (summarized year‑over‑year) format when helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Present changes in a tabular format (e.g., a table that summarizes year‑over‑year changes) to help readers see trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables are recommended for clarity, especially when multiple line items or drivers contribute to changes; tabular presentation can supplement narrative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere repetition of financial statement captions
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A should not merely repeat what is on the face of the financial statements — it should analyze the events, transactions, and economic changes that materially affected reported amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the underlying story 'through the eyes of management' and the implications for future performance rather than a restatement of numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss inflationary impacts and mitigation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If inflation or price changes are part of a known trend or uncertainty reasonably likely to have a material impact, identify principal factors contributing to inflationary pressures, quantify the impact on cost of goods sold and gross margin (if material), and disclose actions planned or taken to mitigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify effects where practicable and update disclosures (including in interim filings) to show ongoing impact; explain any links to revenue, margins, pricing, or promotional activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose effects of supply‑chain disruptions and mitigation consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If supply‑chain issues materially affect results or capital resources, specify whether they have materially impacted results, quantify impacts to sales/profits/liquidity to the extent possible, and discuss known trends or uncertainties resulting from mitigation efforts and any new material risks those efforts introduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe impacts on outlook, business goals, product quality, reliability, or regulatory approvals where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate, industry‑relevant metrics to tell the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate metrics (e.g., same‑store sales, average subscribers) common to the industry to help 'tell the story', while distinguishing such metrics from non‑GAAP adjusted measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the definition and relevance of industry metrics and ensure they are not presented in a way that misleads or disguises GAAP results; see Section 3.4.9 for non‑GAAP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit earliest year only when properly incorporated by reference and not necessary to understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If presenting three years of audited financial statements, registrants may omit discussion of the earliest year only if that discussion exists in a prior EDGAR filing and is properly incorporated by reference; cannot omit if such prior discussion is necessary to understanding financial condition or results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When omitting, disclose the location of the prior discussion. Consider effects of retrospective changes (corrections, accounting changes) when deciding whether omission is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidity sufficiency disclosure (short‑ and long‑term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the registrant believes it has sufficient cash and other liquidity available to fund operations and meet obligations on both a short‑term and long‑term basis (long‑term = greater than 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address capital needs for the next 12 months, material uncertainties around liquidity, and possible impacts on the business (Item 303(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze primary drivers of operating cash flows (not recitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide analysis of the primary drivers and material factors affecting operating cash flows (not just net income and working capital line items), and explain the reasons underlying changes in operating assets and liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make period‑to‑period comparable analyses and discuss factors that actually affected cash rather than simply referencing statement of cash flows captions (see Release No. 33‑8350).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose material cash requirements and anticipated funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose material cash requirements as of the latest fiscal period, the anticipated source(s) of funds needed to satisfy those requirements, and the general purpose of such requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material cash requirements can include capital expenditures, human capital, IP, contractual obligations, and off‑balance‑sheet items. Provide timing and general purpose; although contractual obligation tables are no longer required, provide an analysis of material cash requirements from known contractual and other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize available liquidity by borrowing capacity and other sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider summarizing total available sources of liquidity by type of borrowing capacity, showing capacity less borrowings outstanding, and adding cash/securities to arrive at total available liquidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not presented, disclose where aggregate liquidity information may be found. The SEC staff may request a table or similar summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose key liquidity indicators and metrics management uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include key liquidity indicators (e.g., leverage ratios) and other metrics that management uses to track liquidity so investors understand how management monitors liquidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider metrics meaningful to the business and disclose any significant changes and implications for covenants or liquidity stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider liquidity factors affecting MD&A (leverage, funding availability, sources/uses, intraperiod debt, restrictions, covenant effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A should take into account how factors such as changes in leverage strategies, availability of previously reliable funding, sources and uses of funds, intraperiod debt levels, restrictions on cash flows between parent and subsidiaries, and impacts on debt covenants affect liquidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address significant debt instruments, guarantees, related covenants, and the effects of material cash balances on liquidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical accounting estimates — explain uncertainty, changes, and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: For each critical accounting estimate (CAE), clearly discuss why the CAE is subject to uncertainty, how much the CAE or assumption has changed during the relevant period (if material and reasonably available), and the sensitivity of reported amounts to the methods, assumptions, and estimates underlying the CAE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not merely duplicate footnote accounting policies. Provide methods used, accuracy of past estimates, extent of change, drivers of variability, which assumptions are reasonably likely to change, and quantitative sensitivity analysis when reasonable. See Item 303(b)(3) and Instruction 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight CAEs used in valuations and provide detailed assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss CAEs used in valuations (e.g., goodwill impairment, long‑lived assets, income taxes, fair value determinations), identify reporting units, fair value vs book value, goodwill amounts, and provide detailed description of methods and key assumptions and the degree of uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fair value does not substantially exceed book value, identify reporting unit and disclose percent excess, goodwill allocated, how key assumptions were determined, sensitivity, and potential events that could negatively affect assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate‑related matters when reasonably likely to be material
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider climate‑related matters and their impact on current or future operations and disclose them in MD&A if they meet the Item 303(b)(2)(ii) threshold of being known trends or uncertainties reasonably likely to have a material impact on revenues or income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider whether climate matters require disclosure as risk factors under Item 105. Disclose consistent with SEC interpretive guidance and any applicable final rules (noting regulatory status and litigation developments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Market risk disclosures — quantitative and qualitative information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative and qualitative information about market risk exposures (interest rate, foreign exchange, commodity, equity price risk) associated with market‑sensitive instruments as of fiscal year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three acceptable presentation alternatives: (1) tabular presentation of instruments and contract terms, (2) sensitivity analysis assessing potential loss from hypothetical changes, or (3) value‑at‑risk analysis specifying likelihood. If sensitivity analysis is used, disclose the model description, assumptions, inputs/parameters, and consider multiple hypothetical scenarios (e.g., −100, +/−50, +/−200 bps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose derivatives usage and impact in market risk presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss how derivatives are used to manage market risks, any changes in strategy during the periods presented, and quantify the impact derivatives had on managing interest rate or other risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether sensitivity or EVE outputs reflect the impact of derivatives and provide analysis supporting decisions to omit particular disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe models, assumptions, inputs, and changes over time for risk measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully describe and define inputs and assumptions supporting market risk presentations and sensitivity disclosures and disclose how assumptions or data sources have changed from period to period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include whether proprietary or third‑party data are used, how data are used in modeling, and any unique facts affecting model behavior. Explain changes to assumptions/data due to market conditions or management judgment refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sensitivity analysis where reasonably possible for estimates and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: When reasonably likely changes in assumptions, judgments, or estimates would have a material effect, include qualitative and quantitative sensitivity analysis of reported results to those changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative sensitivity analysis is expected when registrants can reasonably obtain the information; otherwise provide qualitative discussion of potential effects and ranges.
